chapter: Erroll Garner, the 1952 arrest and Florida
title: Out on bail: Herman Chittison and Clarence Williams's daughter in Florida
summary: With Chittison he played Miami clubs for the 1952-53 season.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: And while I was out on bail I joined Herman Chittison and went to Florida. The Court said I could go anywhere I wanted to as long as I was out on bail, just as long as I was in Court on my due date. So I went to Miami during the '52-'53 Season, you know, winter, Hialeah, '52 going into '53, that's the season, you know, in the winter, and I played Mother Kelly's and Clarence Williams, the legendary Clarence Williams, pianist, he's in all these books, his daughter, Irene Williams, was singing with the group. And she was personable. And Herman Chittison was trying to keep her away from everyone, for himself, you know. He's an old man, you know, and he wanted this young girl, and he hired her because
she was young and pretty. So one night we were -- we had left the Mother Collins Club and moved down to the next block.
You said Mother Collins or Mother Kelly?
